01

Setting specification

Task

Compare the $t$-step Lanczos function approximation $y_t=V_t h(T_t)V_t^*b$ with the best approximation in $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)$, under $T_t=V_t^*AV_t$.

Admissible model

The matrix $A\in\mathbb{C}^{d\times d}$ is Hermitian positive definite with actual condition number $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(A)/\lambda_{\min}(A)>1$ and at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues; $1\le t<d$. Also $b\ne0$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$. The function class consists of $h$ or functions whose $z\mapsto h(z)/z$ is Stieltjes: it admits the representation $\int_0^\infty(z+s)^{-1}\,d\nu(s)$ with positive measure $\nu$ satisfying $\int_0^\infty(1+s)^{-1}\,d\nu(s)<\infty$.

Oracle interface

The data $d,t,\kappa,\alpha,h,b$ are public and $A$ is hidden. For any complex vector $v$, the interface returns exact $Av$. Internal complex arithmetic and scalar function evaluations are free.

Output

Return the fixed algorithm's $y_t$. Substituting the best Krylov approximation would change the object being evaluated.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Define the weighted norm $\|z\|_{A^\alpha}=(z^*A^\alpha z)^{1/2}$ and Krylov space $\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)=\operatorname{span}\{b,Ab,\ldots,A^{t-1}b\}$. Compare the fixed Lanczos output with the best approximation in that space through the error ratio $$ \mathcal{C}=\frac{\|h(A)b-y_t\|_{A^\alpha}}{\min_{y\in\mathcal{K}_t(A,b)}\|h(A)b-y\|_{A^\alpha}}. $$. Use the conventions $0/0=1$ and positive numbers divided by zero equal $+\infty$.

Resource accounting

The quantity is the dimensionless approximation factor $\mathcal{C}$, not the minimum query count for a target tolerance. The algorithm uses at most $t$ exact matrix-vector products. Internal arithmetic and scalar-function evaluations are uncharged.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

The exact Lanczos function-approximation algorithm is fixed, without minimization over general algorithms. Equivalent orthonormal-basis implementations are allowed if they produce the same mathematical approximation.

The upper bound holds deterministically for every admissible fixed input. The lower bound concerns worst-case inputs for the fixed algorithm. The supremum over admissible inputs gives the stated sharp factor, generally through arbitrarily close lower examples.

Budget convention
For fixed t, Lanczos uses at most t matrix actions and possibly fewer under early termination. The native comparison target is an error factor.

Complexity bracket

Each bracket applies to the stated view, success guarantee, resource and parameter region. Status summarizes the documented comparisons.

Compared quantities and resource definitions

Q1 · fixed budget risk

\[\sup_{A,h,b}C\!\left(h,A,b,t,\|\cdot\|_{A^\alpha}\right)\]
Scope
The algorithm is fixed to exact single-start Lanczos-FA. For the given d, κ, t, and α, take the supremum of the error approximation factor over all admissible A, h, and b. There is no infimum over algorithms and no conversion to minimum query complexity at a prescribed tolerance.
Optimization direction
minimize
R1Optimal

Nondegenerate Lanczos approximation factor

Parameter region
Assume $\kappa>1$, integers $t\ge1$ and $d\ge t+1$, and $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$. The input matrix has at least $t+1$ distinct eigenvalues.
Success guarantee
The deterministic instancewise criterion compares fixed-Lanczos error with the smallest error in the same Krylov space $K_t$. For each admissible $A$, the lower bound selects suitable $h,b$; it is not a lower bound for every $h,b$.
Quantity
Q1
Resource
Worst-case approximation factor of the fixed algorithm over admissible inputs.
Lower bound

Optimal near-optimality bounds for the Lanczos method for matrix functions ↗
Algorithm scope
The exact Lanczos function-approximation algorithm is fixed, without minimization over general algorithms. Equivalent orthonormal-basis implementations are allowed if they produce the same mathematical approximation.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Exact $Av$ access for a complex Hermitian positive definite matrix. Queries follow the fixed single-start Lanczos recurrence initialized at public $b$; they are not chosen by a general algorithm.
Guarantee conversion
Fully deterministic. The upper bound holds for every instance. For a suitable A, the lower bound provides h and b achieving any factor 1-eta; letting eta tend to zero gives a supremum, without claiming equality on every instance.
Output rule
The output must be the fixed Lanczos-FA value f_t. Compare its A^α-norm error with the minimum error in the same K_t(A,b), using the convention 0/0 = 1.
Resource conversion
The native comparison quantity is the dimensionless approximation factor $\mathcal C$, not the minimum query count needed for a tolerance. The algorithm uses at most $t$ exact matrix–vector products. Internal arithmetic and scalar function evaluations are free.
Constants
Universal constants, with only the parameter dependence permitted by this bound’s region and expression.
Derivation
For each $0<\zeta\le1$, Theorem 2 supplies an admissible input attaining the stated factor times $(1-\zeta)$. Letting $\zeta\downarrow0$ gives the lower bound on the supremum approximation ratio. A finite instance need not attain the supremum exactly.
Upper bound
\[\frac12(\kappa^{E/2}+\kappa^{-E/2}),\quad E=\max\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\]
